# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: US-UPD-01 (United States)
- Period: week 13 (starting 2026-03-30)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift estimates that the AI's catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) at this clinic fell to 68% (band 53% to 82%), compared with a baseline of 90%. This estimate is predicted from 50 scans from this week alone. Expert grades for these scans have not yet arrived.

## 4. Potential patient impact
If the estimate is correct, approximately 2.87818 referable cases may have been missed. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
A drop in the referral rate (0.360 compared with 0.685 in training) across 50 scans suggests a potential shift towards a lower-risk patient population, although visual artifacts in flagged images make this evidence weak and inconclusive (category: patient population shift; confidence 45%; source: gemini).

Evidence:
- Referral rate decreased from 0.685 in training to 0.360 in week 13 (a relative change of -0.474) across 50 scans.
- Mean referral score changed from 0.193 in training to 0.188 (a relative change of -0.023).
- Aggregate image metrics do not show degradation: mean quality is 0.529 compared with 0.500 in training, mean sharpness is 0.000457 compared with 0.000399 in training, mean brightness is 0.361 compared with 0.373 in training, and mean contrast is 0.0954 compared with 0.0963 in training.
- Visual inspection of sample flagged images shows artifacts such as dark peripheral vignetting in Scan 1 and central glare in Scan 2, rendering the evidence for a population shift weak and mixed with image quality concerns.

## 6. Action
Expected harm: 104348. Cost of review: 25000.
As the expected harm exceeds the cost of review, we recommend pausing the AI at this clinic and sending its scans for human grading until the checks below are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Audit patient intake demographics and risk profiles for week 13 to confirm whether the patient mix changed.
- [ ] Inspect the camera lens and optical path for smudges, dust, or alignment issues that could cause vignetting or glare.
- [ ] Re-train clinic operators on patient positioning and eye alignment to prevent scans containing artifacts.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm forms part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response must fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
